before:
very low (straight line/schematic): route is a straight line or schematic — a basic point A to point B connection, not an actual alignment
low: route follows the general path of the actual alignment, but is only coarsely or partially traced
medium: route is not a straight line, but hasn't been traced
high: route has been digitally traced in GIS software or the shapefile has been obtained from a reliable source
very high (within meters): route has been traced to within meters of the actual alignment
no route: we don't have a route for it, either because it's unavailable/unknown or is a capacity/directionality expansion
